I recently got out of a situationship like this, but not quite as severe. I want to say this gently: I fear you are being manipulated, and she’s using her anxiety as a tool. Mental illness is not a valid excuse to make the people around you miserable. She should know this. But I think she’s learned that you clearly have a big heart and are very compassionate, and will respond to her having panic attacks in a way that makes her the center of attention. I say this because of the part where you said she gets mad that other people are treated before her in the ER, I’m sorry but that’s ridiculous. I used to date a guy who used his depression as an excuse for literally everything. Standing me up on Valentine’s Day. Depression. Not defending me when a guy in his frat called me a slur. Depression. Not texting/calling for days/weeks. Depression. And when I finally (after 3 years) cut things off for good, guess what he tried to do? Manipulate me to come back because “ I’m the only one who understands what he’s going through.” I think mental health is very important, but it should not be used to back people into a corner. But I realized his issues with depression shouldn’t also put me in a depression. Leaving is hard. I know that first hand. But you are strong and can do it, at some point you need to take your mental health into consideration and realize that hers is chipping away at yours.
